transcript.note: Round 1. All 10 already-H/V segments are the frozen prescribed square (verts 0,3,4,6,7,11,13,14,15,16), so only 1,2,5,8,9,10,12 can move and every off-segment has at least one frozen end. Worked component by component. (a) Vertex 8 is degree-4 with all four neighbours frozen at (1,5)/(13,8)/(8,13)/(9,1); the required rows are 5/8/13/1 and columns 1/13/8/9, all distinct, so one point can satisfy at most one row plus one column — chose the pair reachable in one short move: 8 (6,9)->(8,8) closes 8-16 into H (row 8) and 8-3 into V (column 8), +2. (b) 16-10 is a 45 degree that must be upgraded, and column 13 is forbidden because a vertical 16-10 would lie on top of the ring edge 16-14; so 10 (14,7)->(14,8) makes it H on row 8, and 12 (16,6)->(16,8) puts the whole 16-10-12 chain on that same row, +2 (criterion 3, align a chain rather than single segments). (c) The tail 1-9-5-3 hangs off frozen 3 (8,13): H for 5-3 would need row 13, which puts 5 on top of the ring segment 15-3, so took V instead - 5 (7,14)->(8,14), then 9 (10,15)->(8,15) keeps 9-5 vertical on the same column 8, and 1 (4,16)->(4,15) closes 1-9 into H on row 15; folding the tail onto one column instead of one row also avoids 1-9 swallowing vertex 5, +3. Checked winding order by hand at every degree>=3 neighbour (4, 16, 3, 7) before proposing: the bearing sequences stay in the same circular order. 7-2 deliberately left alone - row 1 would swallow frozen vertex 14 and column 9 is 6 cells away. Expect 10 -> 17 of 20.
